the development of a new generation of computer graphics techniques for the display of large amounts of four-dimensional meteorlogical data in a way that is more effective than conventional methods.
the design and implementation of interactive, animated, stereo display terminals for meteorological data.
how to make the computer display look like the real world, not the other way around.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the computer-generated imagery for 3-D meteorological data is a very effective tool for meteorological data analysis.
the use of these image generation techniques has resulted in a dramatic improvement in the ability of meteorologists to visualize and interpret four-dimensional meteorological phenomena.
computer-generated imagery can be an effective tool in presenting four-dimensional data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have learned that the best way to display four-dimensional data is to display as much of it as possible, and then let the user sort it out.
we are using computer-generated imagery to create the illusion of a three-dimensional world in which we can interact with the atmosphere.
the images have proven extremely effective in conveying the dynamic structure of the atmosphere and in providing a new way of visualizing and understanding meteorological data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human visual system can be a valuable aid in the analysis of large amounts of data.
it is not necessary to create a completely new display technique for each type of meteorological data, but rather to use the display geometry and the animation to enhance the data.
it is possible to generate computer-generated images of meteorological data which are both aesthetically pleasing and scientifically useful.
